QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_37

question.text: Mr. Aakash Verma, Head of Investments at Sahyadri Capital AIF (Cat II), resigns. His role is pivotal and he led 70% of portfolio IC decisions. Under Regulation 22 transparency norms, what is the Manager's obligation?

answer.text: No disclosure required; employment matters are internal.
Disclose only at the next annual general meeting of LPs (180-day report).
Disclose as a 'significant change in the key investment team' to LPs per Regulation 22(g), as and when it occurs.
Disclose only to SEBI in the next T+10 quarterly filing, not to LPs.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 22 expressly requires transparency and disclosure to investors on (g) 'any significant change in the key investment team,' as and when it occurs. A departure of the Head of Investments who led 70% of IC decisions is unambiguously significant. The Trap: 'Internal matter' (A) ignores the express regulation. Batching to annual / quarterly (B, D) misses the 'as and when' trigger. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C identical. On XIX-A distributor exam, the LP-side twin question asks what rights the client can invoke on such disclosure (often, a material-change exit). Manager's Pro-Tip: Your PPM should define 'Key Persons' by name AND specify triggers (e.g., if 2 of 3 Key Persons leave, investment period suspends). LPs will ask for this clause — absence of a Key Person clause is a red flag in LP diligence.
